title: Decide whether you are adding, challenging, or translating
use_cases: Configure when adapting legacy content with outdated or harmful assumptions
Implement when choosing between adding context, challenging material, or translating platforms
Use when establishing a critical frame to inform existing fanbase expectations
Configure when balancing original work preservation with modern inclusive values
content:
Ethics in adaptation are not abstract. They determine whether your work feels like thoughtful engagement or opportunistic extraction. Ask a simple question: are you adding context, challenging the source, or translating it for a new platform and audience? Each of those goals is valid, but they imply different responsibilities. If you are challenging the source, you should state that openly so fans understand the critical frame.

This matters especially when the original work contains outdated, exclusionary, or harmful assumptions. A responsible reinterpretation can expose those assumptions without pretending they were never there. That balance is what makes adaptation ethics so important for creators who want to earn trust from both fans and newcomers. In practice, it means acknowledging the source’s legacy while still making room for a more inclusive reading. The goal is not to erase the original; the goal is to contextualize it honestly.
